items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Oh yeah. I remember seeing that. [?] for Pablo. Norman Granz [?]. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. Norman Granz did it.

ctx.x: Then he turned around to me and laughed. Oh man. Then Sweet Georgia Brown is so fast, it’s unbelievable. Only he can play at those tempos. But I enjoyed working with Oscar, too. He was a giant musician. He could really play. Speaking of tapes, the next to last thing that Duke recorded was something we did out in California. I played drums. Joe Pass is on guitar and Ray Brown on bass and Duke. Just the four of us. You know about that one? He called it Duke’s Big Four.
Oh yeah. I remember seeing that. [?] for Pablo. Norman Granz [?].

Yeah. Norman Granz did it. Yeah. Norman did it. Pat Williard, I think, has a copy of that tape. That’s unbelievable. Duke had never heard Joe Pass play. He kept saying, “What’s that guy’s name?” Joe Pass. Joe Passalaqua is his real name. Joe Pass. He said, “Man, that guy could . . .” He was overcome with Joe Pass. Never heard anything like it. That’s [?]. It’s good. It’s a videotape. I asked you about that. She’s got the only copy of it. I may have a copy of it. I think I do have a copy of it. It’s been sitting…
